item.title: The Language Equation
item.description: A conversation with Patrick McGinty on new language, narration, and queer identity in his new novel “Town College City Road.”

item.title: In Search of Lost Process; or, How I Wrote My First Book
item.description: “I was young, full of creative energy, filling black notebooks with pressed ballpoint ink. Time dilated because I was unbothered by the reality of lugging my dirty laundry down to the laundromat every few weeks or eating rice and beans day after day.”

item.description: “Every city is about change—even Pittsburgh, which for so long we thought of as stuck or static.”

item.title: Unruly Humor: Damon Young on the Truth in Black Humor
item.description: “That this is bloody and Black-as-fuck honesty is where the best comedy is born. It’s lowbrow. It’s midbrow, it’s highbrow. It’s every brow.”

item.title: “Art is [still] a Weapon”: A Brief History of the Protest Novel
item.description: “Every time he saw another building in Pittsburgh being spray washed to remove the decades of soot… he would think of their legacies being slowly erased.”
